```{python}
# Include and execute your code here
# Don't forget, you need another import statement to import the desired ML model from sklearn
from sklearn.ensemble import RandomForestClassifier
from sklearn.metrics import classification_report, confusion_matrix, ConfusionMatrixDisplay
from sklearn.inspection import permutation_importance
import polars.selectors as cs

x = df.select(cs.numeric().exclude(["before1980","yrbuilt"]))
y = df.select("before1980")

x_train, x_test, y_train, y_test = train_test_split(x, y, test_size=0.2, random_state=28)

rf_classifier = RandomForestClassifier()
rf_classifier.fit(x_train, y_train)

rf_pred = rf_classifier.predict(x_test)

print(classification_report(y_test, rf_pred))

rf_cm=confusion_matrix(y_test, rf_pred)
rf_disp = ConfusionMatrixDisplay(confusion_matrix = rf_cm)

ConfusionMatrixDisplay.from_estimator(rf_classifier, x_test, y_test, cmap="Greens")
```


## QUESTION 2

1. __Justify your classification model by discussing the most important features selected by your model.__ This discussion should include a plot of permutation importance values for the most important features. Were there any features you thought would be importance but weren't?

The most important feature selected by my model was if the house had an attached garage, followed by the number of stories and the number of baths. I'm not surprised by any of the non-important entries as I did extensive data mapping in the last task.

```{python}
# Include and execute your code here
rf_result= permutation_importance(rf_classifier, x_test, y_test, n_repeats=4,random_state=28)

rf_perms_imp = pl.DataFrame({'importance':rf_result.importances_mean, 'vars':x_train.columns})

with pl.Config(tbl_rows=-1, tbl_cols=-1, fmt_str_lengths=1000):
    display(
      print(rf_perms_imp.sort(['importance'], descending=True))
    )

```

```{python}
(
  ggplot(rf_perms_imp.filter(pl.col("importance") > 0).sort("importance", descending=True), aes(x="vars", y="importance"))
  +geom_bar(stat="identity", position="dodge")
  +labs(x="Attributes", y="Importance", title="Importance of attributes at guessing homes built before 1980")
  +ggsize(2500, 1250)
)
```

## QUESTION 3

1. __For the 3 most important features, explain their relationship to the target variable. Use a plot to illustrate the relationship.__ (3 plots minimum)

All three of the highest scored attributes show a clear upward trend over the years. The one that starts the lowest and climbs the most is the attached garage, and the number of bathrooms has a fairly steady trend up until the 80s. Honestly I'm not sure why stories is such a good predictor when it starts out higher than the 80s and then dips down before coming back up. I assumed that having two areas on opposite sides of the target year would muddy up the data, but it appears not!

```{python}
# Include and execute your code here
df_garage = df.group_by("yrbuilt").agg(gar_proportion = pl.col("gartype_Att").sum() / pl.col("totunits").sum()).sort("yrbuilt", descending=True)
df_stories = df.group_by("yrbuilt").agg(stories_avg = pl.col("stories").mean()).sort("yrbuilt", descending=True)
df_numbaths = df.group_by("yrbuilt").agg(baths_avg = pl.col("numbaths").mean()).sort("yrbuilt", descending=True)
```
```{python}
(
  ggplot(df_garage, aes(x="yrbuilt", y="gar_proportion"))
  +geom_line()
  +labs(x="Year Built", y="Proportion of Homes With Attached Garages")

)
```

```{python}
)
```
